quality_verdict: Judged on llvmpipe renders under the contact-sheet light (measured); how it looks on Steam Deck or real GPUs is inferred. Good: the player car's rear, which is on screen the whole race, now behaves like the sprite at night: the whole tail lamp glows, braking is a clear step, the third brake light and plate are lit. Nothing pokes into the tyres any more, the bumpers end in rounded corners, the kompakt shoulder is clean, and discs and rims read as metal. Traffic cars at 10-80 m look more like real cars: dark rims, glossy glass, lid seams, badge, exhaust pipe, and a grey plate that survives to lod2. The 40 m swap is now mostly the plate glyphs (6.6-9.8 % of pixels, measured). The truck's red/yellow contour is now the strongest night cue. Not yet: paint still looks flat and over-exposed (kompakt yellow, white truck), and unlit lamps look switched on by day. Both are shader/light issues (R3) that no mesh change fixes. Traffic tail lamps are still flat stickers without lens depth (B2). At 120 m the lod1->lod2 swap still changes 22-34 % of a car's pixels, a visible pop. In the showroom the real-time cars are clearly below the sprite (paint, glass), so the flag stays false. Missing: wagon lod2 third-brake-light shape, A8/A9 lamp details, truck cab rework (AS2b), far-lamp glow (F6).
